newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bewag sees slightly higher 1996/97 profit. [CORRECTED 12:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bewag sees slightly higher 1996/97 profit. [CORRECTED 12:30 GMT]

text.p: German utility group BEWAG AG said on Thursday that it expected to report a profit of between 170 million and 180 million marks ($106.2 million) for the year to June 30, 1997, marginally above its 1995/96 profit of 169 million marks.
Berliner Kraft- und Licht AG (Bewag) chief financial officer Bernd Balzereit said the slight improvement in profit came despite falling sales in electricity and heating.
The utility group posted a pretax profit of 359 million marks ($211.7 million) for the first nine months of the current business year, down from 372 million marks in 1995/96.
Balzereit noted however that the profit figure improved by 155 million marks if extraordinary writedowns were stripped out.
Its nine-month sales eased to 3.158 billion marks from 3.326 billion. Sales in 1995/96 totalled 4.428 billion marks.

Balzereit said the company had a long-term plan to distribute a larger proportion of its profits to its shareholder owners in future. For 1996/97, the company plans to distribute 45 percent of its profits, paying a one mark dividend per five-mark nominal value share.
He said this would be increased to around 40 percent following the company's privatisation.
The Berlin government agreed last week to sell 50.8 percent of Bewag to Veba AG's subsidiary PreussenElektra, Viag AG and Southern Co of the United States.
